newsitem.title: USA: New rules bar 13.7 mln acres now in U.S. CRP - study.
newsitem.headline: New rules bar 13.7 mln acres now in U.S. CRP - study.

text.p: Some 13.7 million acres now enrolled in the Conservation Reserve would not meet at least one of the criteria for entry under new Agriculture Department rules, an analysis said Monday.

The analysis by the Food and Agricultural Policy Research Institute at the University of Missouri said the stricter erodibility requirements proposed n the rules would preclude at least some land from re-enrollment.
USDA proposed the new rules last week. They would not take effect until after a 45-day period for comment and suggested changes.
Land would be required to have an erodibility index of at least eight to be eligible in the future or meet some other standard such as being devoted to wellhead protection or a filterstrip.
FAPRI said about three million acres that did not have an erodibility index of eight but were devoted to those practices.
The think tank said 73 percent of the CRP land in Missouri met the erodibility index test.
It listed other states as Iowa 69 percent, Texas 63 percent, Kansas and Illinois 61 percent, North Dakota 57 percent, Indiana 55 percent, South Dakota 53 percent, and Oklahoma 51 percent.

States with high percentages of land meeting the erodibility test were Wyoming 98 percent, Kentucky 90 percent, Colorado 89 percent, Tennessee 83 percent, Wisconsin 78 percent, Montana 77 percent and Nebraska 74 percent.
Contracts on 24 million acres expire by fall 1997.
FAPRI based its estimates on a sampling of CRP land.
